issues.description: Identity-based service comparison uses `==` rather than `is`, risking subtle equality surprises
issues.detail: In `service_switcher.py`, the guard `if frame.service == self.strategy.active_service` compares two `FrameProcessor` instances with `==`. The intent is clearly object identity (the same processor instance), not structural equality. If `FrameProcessor` ever overrides `__eq__` (or a subclass does), this becomes a latent bug where the wrong frame is consumed or leaks through. Use `is` for identity comparison; that is also the invariant the surrounding logic relies on.

issues.description: Holding a live `FrameProcessor` reference on a control frame creates a lifetime/coupling hazard
issues.detail: `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame.service: FrameProcessor` embeds a processor instance into a frame that flows through the pipeline. This couples a data-class control message to a graph node, prevents serialization, complicates testing, and risks keeping a swapped-out service alive via the frame queue. A more rigorous design would target by a stable identifier (service name/id) and let the switcher resolve identity, preserving the invariant 'consume iff this frame was addressed to the currently active service' without leaking a node reference into the frame stream.

issues.description: Loop/branch invariant for the suppression rule is not stated in code
issues.detail: The new `push_frame` logic encodes a non-trivial invariant: 'a `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` is consumed exactly once, by the switcher that owns the targeted active service; all others must let it pass.' That invariant is implicit. A one-line literate comment stating it (and why the inactive-service case must not be suppressed) would make the correctness argument legible to a reader who has not seen the prior PR.

issues.description: Frame ordering contract (metadata before request frame) is implicit and untested
issues.detail: Both `STTService` and `MockMetadataService` now do `await self._push_..._metadata(); await self.push_frame(frame, direction)`. The order matters: downstream must see the metadata before (or at least not after a delayed) request frame, and the switcher relies on the request frame still being in flight to consume it. There is no test asserting this ordering invariant, and no comment stating it. A small assertion in `test_metadata_emitted_on_service_switch` that the `MockMetadataFrame` precedes the `ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame` in `processed_frames` would lock the contract.

issues.description: Forward-reference string `"FrameProcessor"` without an import guard invites a NameError at dataclass introspection time
issues.detail: `service: "FrameProcessor"` is a forward reference, but `FrameProcessor` is not imported in `frames.py` (presumably to avoid a cycle). That is fine for runtime construction, but any code that calls `typing.get_type_hints(ServiceSwitcherRequestMetadataFrame)` or a Pydantic-style resolver will fail. Either add a `TYPE_CHECKING`-guarded import so the annotation resolves under `get_type_hints`, or type it as `Any` with a comment explaining the cycle. Quietly storing an unresolvable annotation is the kind of thing that bites a year later.

review.summary: The change is small, localized, and the algorithmic intent is sound: route a metadata-refresh request to exactly one service and let the switcher consume the frame only when it was addressed to the currently active service. Decision label: UNDER-AUDITED, leaning RIGOROUS once two issues are tightened. The core invariant — 'consume the request frame iff `frame.service` is this switcher's active service' — should be stated in a comment and enforced with `is` rather than `==`, because identity, not equality, is what the design depends on. Embedding a live `FrameProcessor` reference in a control frame is the most questionable data-structure choice here; targeting by stable id keeps the frame a value object and avoids lifetime coupling. The ordering contract (push metadata, then the request frame) is load-bearing for the switcher's suppression rule and deserves both a comment and a direct test assertion. No performance concerns; this is firmly in the 97% where premature optimization would be the wrong instinct.
